title: Comparison inverse image commutes with scheme pullback
statement:
For $u:U\to V$ there is a natural isomorphism

$$
 \nu_U^*u_{\Et}^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 u_{\Proet}^{-1}\nu_V^*.
$$

It is compatible with identity maps, composites, and the cartesian
identification in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

proof.text: Apply injectivity of conjugateIsoEquiv to the identity and composition equations for the canonical inverse-image comparisons. The conjugation rules for composition, whiskering, associators and unitors turn their two sides into the corresponding equations between restriction direct images. Evaluate those transformations at a sheaf G and an etale object W. Unfold the restriction comparison and the canonical fibre-product identity or associativity maps; all comparison components are identity maps. Functoriality removes the identity factors. In the identity case, the etale and pro-etale pullback identity maps are the same scheme morphism. In the composition case, the etale and pro-etale pullback associativity maps are the same scheme morphism. Both remaining equations are therefore reflexive. Taking hom components of the resulting natural-isomorphism equations gives the identity and composition clauses for every sheaf and every coefficient category with the stated adjunctions.

proof.text: For the specified Cartesian square, expand each square identification as the inverse composition comparison for (f',g), followed by eqToIso along the supplied commutativity equality, followed by the composition comparison for (g',f). The comparison is compatible with transport along equality of scheme morphisms: prove this by substituting equal morphisms, after which both transports are identities. Apply the two composition equations established in step 3 and this transport equation. Cancel the composition isomorphisms to obtain the square equation as an equality of natural isomorphisms, retaining precisely the supplied equality sq.w. This cancellation and whiskering calculation is proved in arbitrary categories before specialization to the etale and pro-etale inverse-image functors. Evaluating hom components gives exactly the componentwise square clause. The generic proof applies to sets, abelian groups, and modules over each finite discrete ring; conjoin these three specializations to obtain the stated theorem.
